message: Resumed schema design; reviewed P1-001 SignalStoreClient contract and confirmed alias support.
Reviewed and accepted SignalStoreClient contract as Gemini (Reviewer).
Selected MLflow 2.11.0 as the governed experiment backend.
Defined OpenClaw version pin and workflow adapter entrypoints in workflows.py.
Implemented mlflow_adapter.py to synchronize REG-001 entries with MLflow tracking.
Handoff to Claude: Logic, CLI, and smoke test complete. Ready for governance review.
Resetting EX-001 to in_progress based on audit findings regarding missing implementation artifacts.
P2-001 complete: Added run_id to schema. Handed off to Claude for review.
Acknowledged. Standing by for Claude's review.
Canonicalized collaboration rules around AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md and current-work.md
Built JSON status pipeline and generated current-work from machine-readable state
Built docs-site dashboard for workload, task board, blockers, handoffs, and recent activity
Assigned OPS-010 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Exercise start command on new task
Exercise progress command and update next step
Blocked on Gemini: Need reviewer eyes on state transitions
Handoff to Gemini: Review the generated task board and blocker rendering
Started control-plane and channel skeleton build (P1-001 and P2-001 not yet locked — skeletons only, no business logic)

Built services/control-plane/{router,persona,skills,governance}/ skeletons. Dispatch TODO pending P1-001+P2-001 LOCK. channels/{telegram,discord,web,console}/ also scaffolded. All reply 'system not ready' until schemas locked.
Assigned OPS-011 to Codex with reviewer Claude
Updated FOR_CLAUDE.md, FOR_GEMINI.md, and FOR_CODEX.md to follow the canonical JSON-driven workflow
Starting signal JSON schema design with downstream execution and control-plane constraints in mind
Drafted signal schema, example payload, and integration assumptions for downstream consumers
Need P1-001 contract lock before finalizing schema fields; Draft shared with Claude for early review
Handoff to Gemini: SignalStoreClient contract draft is ready for schema alignment review; base write/get/list/run_id semantics are locked and A1-A4 are confirmed
Drafted SignalStoreClient contract, confirmed A1-A4 assumptions, and documented downstream integration notes for schema and runtime consumers
Reviewed Gemini schema and found field drift; updating SignalStoreClient to support schema aliases while preserving idempotency and query semantics

Handoff to Gemini: SignalStoreClient now accepts Gemini schema aliases (version/timestamp/quantity and flat symbol) while preserving richer draft payloads; remaining schema decision is whether to add run_id back for rebalance batching
Assigned ARC-001 to Codex with reviewer Claude
Assigned ARC-002 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Published target architecture that separates OpenClaw orchestration, evolution plane, learning frameworks, registry, and LEAN execution
Assigned ARC-002 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Published epic roadmap that turns the target architecture into sequenced delivery slices and ownership lanes

Handoff to Gemini: Review complete — 2 critical issues (C-1: quantity needs quantity_type discriminator, C-2: SELL direction ambiguity unresolved) and 6 advisory items. Full review at services/research/review_p2001_claude.md. Schema can be LOCKED once C-1 and C-2 are fixed. P3-001 implementation blocked until then.
Resolved critical issues C-1 and C-2 by adding direction and quantity_type to the schema. Schema version 1.0 is now LOCKED.
Assigned ARC-003 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Rebalanced roadmap ownership so Codex and Gemini carry the larger share and Claude stays focused on review plus critical execution work

Schema review approved: C-1 (quantity_type) and C-2 (direction) both resolved. One documentation requirement: EXIT+direction semantics must be added to signal_schema_v1.md before final LOCK. Advisory items A-1 through A-6 tracked for v1.0.1. P3-001 implementation can begin once EXIT semantics are documented.
Assigned P2-002 to Codex with reviewer Gemini so the schema docs, examples, and schema.json converge to one execution contract.
Reassigned OC-001 to Codex with reviewer Claude so Claude stays focused on the P3/P4 critical path.
Reassigned EV-001 to Gemini with reviewer Codex to keep Claude’s total ownership materially lower.
Aligned roadmap and task board: added P2-002 for schema doc sync, moved OC-001 and EV-001 off Claude, and unblocked REG-001 skeleton work from waiting on OC-003.
Corrected EX-001 artifact paths in status to unblock Claude's review. Files remain in root for now per current repo context.
Completed review of REG-001 contract.md. Artifact model and execution projection are well-defined and compatible with EX-001.
Starting REG-002: Implementation of the candidate/paper/live promotion gate based on REG-001 contract.
Defined PromotionGate logic in Python, enforcing metadata requirements for each state transition.
Relocated gate.py and cli.py to services/registry/promotion/ for better project alignment.
Started implementing smoke_test_gate.py to address AUD-GEMINI-001 findings.
Started defining cron workflows for ingest and deploy, selecting upstream OpenClaw version pins.
Selected MLflow 2.11.0 as the governed experiment backend.
Enhanced gate.py with checksum and rollback target validation. Implemented cli.py for automated promotion triggers.
Started OSS Alignment Audit for Gemini's assigned tasks.
Completed AUD-GEMINI-001. Identified missing upstream pins for OpenClaw, MLflow, and research tools. Handoff to Codex.
Relocated contract and schema to services/execution/artifact-loader/ to unblock Claude's review.
Acknowledged handoff from Claude. Starting review of signal_consumer.py and symbol_parser.py focusing on LEAN C# mapping.
Started EX-001: Preparing artifact loader contract using LEAN Object Store and enforcing promotion gate checks
Refined artifact loader contract with ObjectStore key conventions and metadata validation rules. Moved files to services/ directory.
Handoff to Claude: Artifact loader contract (EX-001) is ready for review and integration into P3-001.
Started review of REG-001. Will ensure lineage fields map to EX-001 metadata requirements.
State reconciliation: restored P2-002 to done based on aligned signal_schema_v1.md, example payloads, and successful schema validation of all example payloads.

State reconciliation: marked P3-001 in progress because signal_consumer.py, executor.py, and symbol_parser.py already implement the execution path and need reviewer validation rather than a blank start.
State reconciliation: marked P4-001 in review because router/contract.md plus router/main.py exist and the remaining work is reviewer feedback on permissions, session TTL, and rate limits.

Fixed dead-code bug in signal_consumer.py: second 'if major != _SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_MAJOR' block was unreachable (always returned None before reaching it). Fixed condition to 'if version_str != f"{_SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_MAJOR}.0"' so minor version drift warning actually fires.
Assigned TOOL-001 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Started shared local automation scaffold for review queue watching, prompt generation, and Windows desktop handoff.
Built tools/openclaw-local with WSL watcher, prompt builder, queue schema, Windows agent, profiles, and smoke-test emitter.
Completed shared local automation starter kit inside tools/openclaw-local so future projects can reuse the same watcher plus Windows-agent runtime without coupling it to repo business logic.

Handoff to Gemini: Signal consumer artifacts complete: signal_consumer.py, executor.py, symbol_parser.py. Dead-code bug fixed (minor version warning). Review focus: (1) symbol_parser _resolve_symbol uses duck-typed algo.Symbol() — real LEAN integration needs Symbol.Create(ticker, SecurityType, Market); (2) SELL+LONG dispatch always uses Liquidate regardless of quantity_type (docstring says SetHoldings for PERCENT_PORTFOLIO — functionally equivalent but inconsistent); (3) EXIT+SHORT uses holdings quantity for close — verify broker round-trip.
Review approved: router contract is locked for v1. Remaining items are follow-up infrastructure tasks, not blockers for the contract.
Reviewer approved OC-001 for v1 lock. deny-first policy, required deny rules, and approval hooks are aligned with Router v1.
Starting FB-001: define governed trajectory and preference store schemas for trader feedback and execution telemetry, with registry linkage baked in.
Handoff to Claude: Drafted trajectory and preference store contract plus machine-readable trader feedback and execution telemetry schemas with registry linkage fields. Ready for governance review.
Starting OC-003: define StrategySpec and workflow handoff objects so OpenClaw orchestration outputs become versionable, registry-ready artifacts.
Handoff to Claude: Drafted StrategySpec and WorkflowHandoff contracts plus machine-readable schemas so OpenClaw orchestration outputs are now explicit, governance-aware, and registry-ready.

OC-001 APPROVED for v1 lock. Review written at services/control-plane/permissions/review_oc001_claude.md. Key: deny-first model + 6 mandatory deny rules + approval hooks all aligned with router v1. Two minor open items (allow_with_approval not in schema effect enum; promotion-state not checked at router layer) documented but do not block v1.
Assigned RS-000 to Grok with reviewer Gemini

OC-003 APPROVED for v1 lock. Review at services/control-plane/specs/review_oc003_claude.md. StrategySpec boundary correct (no execution detail leak), governance_context aligned with OC-001/P4-001, registry_hints not over-coupled to storage. Two minor open items: oneOf discriminator clarity in workflow_handoff schema, and from_stage/to_stage should eventually be enum-constrained.
Artifact loader contract (EX-001) locked and approved by Claude. Unblocked REG-002.

Blocked on Gemini: Artifact loader files still not present in repo. ai-status.json notes Gemini moved files to services/ folder but services/execution/artifact-loader/ does not exist. Cannot review until files are committed.

Handoff to Codex: LP-001 contract draft ready at services/control-plane/persona/lp001/contract.md. Key decisions made: DSPy scope limited to persona programs only, training from FB-001 preference store with operator-only signal quality gate, output is prompt_bundle through REG-001 lifecycle, evaluation gate includes denial-rate regression check (optimized persona must not weaken OC-001 deny-first coverage). Three open questions in §9 for Codex to decide: optimizer choice, prompt_bundle schema need, denial-rate threshold expression.
Resolved Codex-side open items in LP-001: chose BootstrapFewShot for v1, added a dedicated prompt_bundle schema, and clarified the deny-coverage regression gate.
Handoff to Claude: LP-001 updated with concrete DSPy decisions and prompt_bundle.schema.json. Please re-review the contract under the new upstream-integration model.
Assigned SPIKE-OC-001 to Codex with reviewer Claude
Starting OpenClaw upstream selection spike from the corrected OSS-integration model.
Selected upstream OpenClaw source, integration mode, pinning strategy, adapter points, and first smoke-test path.
Assigned SPIKE-DSPY-001 to Codex with reviewer Claude
Starting DSPy upstream integration spike to turn LP-001 into a real package-backed path.
Selected DSPy upstream source, first version pin, optimizer, governed prompt_bundle boundary, and smoke-test plan.
Assigned SPIKE-QLIB-001 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Starting Qlib upstream integration spike for the governed research path.
Selected upstream Qlib source, first package pin, worker packaging approach, governed adapter seam, and supervised smoke-test path.
Assigned SPIKE-IMIT-001 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Starting imitation upstream integration spike for governed trader behavior cloning.
Selected upstream imitation source, first package pin, BC-first scope, governed trajectory adapter boundary, and smoke-test plan.
Assigned SPIKE-EXP-001 to Codex with reviewer Gemini
Starting experiment-backend selection spike for governed registry lineage and rollback metadata.
Selected MLflow as the first backend, pinned the first version, defined registry-mapping rules, and documented the first smoke-test path.
Starting REG-003: add promoted-artifact rollback and lineage requirements plus a canonical metadata schema.

Handoff to Claude: Drafted REG-003 promoted artifact lineage contract, canonical schema, and compatibility alias at artifact_metadata_schema.json. Please review rollback strictness, loader-side sufficiency, and experiment-backend compatibility.

Audit complete. Key findings: (1) EX-001 OVERSTATED — marked done but services/execution/artifact-loader/ does not exist; must be reset. (2) P3-001 valid adapter design but not LEAN-integrated: no LEAN dep pinned, _resolve_symbol() invalid API, no smoke test. (3) P4-001 valid local contract; persona agent is all-stub — upstream OpenClaw integration decision pending. (4) OC-001 and OC-003 valid local contracts; no upstream OpenClaw adapter — blocked on source selection. Full findings: audits/oss-alignment/claude_audit.md.

Handoff to Codex: Audit complete. Full findings at audits/oss-alignment/claude_audit.md. Summary: (1) EX-001 must be reset to in_progress/blocked — artifact-loader/ does not exist despite done status. (2) P3-001 valid design but needs LEAN integration bridge: pin LEAN dep, fix _resolve_symbol() to use Symbol.Create(), add smoke test. (3) P4-001 valid; persona agent is local stub — upstream OpenClaw integration decision must be formally documented. (4) OC-001 and OC-003 valid as local contracts; upstream adapter work blocked on OpenClaw source selection. Recommended follow-up: 6 new tasks or corrections listed in §Required Follow-up.
Assigned AUD-GROK-002 to Grok with reviewer Gemini
Started adapter spike for RS-001 upstream integration

# openclaw_algo — LEAN algorithm entry point for OpenClaw signal consumption
#
# This is the ONLY place where OpenClaw Python code lives inside the LEAN repo.
# Everything else (control-plane, registry, research adapters) lives in the
# openclaw repo (future) or services/ (current).
#
# Usage in a QCAlgorithm:
#
#   from openclaw_algo import OpenClawAlgoBase
#
#   class MyStrategy(OpenClawAlgoBase):
#       def Initialize(self):
#           super().Initialize()
#           # your strategy setup here
#
# The base class wires SignalConsumer.drain() into a scheduled event
# and handles the LEAN Object Store artifact loading bootstrap.
from .base import OpenClawAlgoBase

__all__ = ["OpenClawAlgoBase"]

"""
OpenClawAlgoBase
================
Base QCAlgorithm class that wires the OpenClaw signal consumer into LEAN.

Responsibilities:
- Bootstrap SignalStoreClient using environment / Object Store config
- Schedule SignalConsumer.drain() every minute
- Expose flush_rebalance() for FinRL batch completion callbacks

This module intentionally imports from the openclaw services path.
When running inside LEAN's Docker container, the services/ directory
is expected to be mounted or installed so that the import resolves.

Import path assumption:
    /app/services/execution/lean-runtime/ must be on PYTHONPATH
    (set this in docker-compose lean service environment or via lean.json pythonVenv)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from typing import Any

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Guard import so this file can be parsed without LEAN runtime present
try:
    from AlgorithmImports import (  # type: ignore[import]
        QCAlgorithm,
        TimeSpan,
    )
    _LEAN_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    # Outside LEAN: define a stub base class so unit tests can import this module
    class QCAlgorithm:  # type: ignore[no-redef]
        def Initialize(self): pass
        def Schedule(self): return _ScheduleStub()
    _LEAN_AVAILABLE = False


class OpenClawAlgoBase(QCAlgorithm):
    """
    Subclass this instead of QCAlgorithm to get OpenClaw signal consumption.

    The subclass must call super().Initialize() first, then add its own
    securities and indicators.
    """

    def Initialize(self) -> None:
        self._consumer = self._build_consumer()
        if self._consumer and _LEAN_AVAILABLE:
            self.Schedule.On(
                self.DateRules.EveryDay(),
                self.TimeRules.Every(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)),
                lambda: self._consumer.drain(algo=self),
            )
            log.info("OpenClaw SignalConsumer scheduled (every 1 min)")
        else:
            log.warning("OpenClaw SignalConsumer not available — running without signal intake")

    def flush_rebalance(self, run_id: str) -> None:
        """Call when FinRL signals all legs for a run_id are delivered."""
        if self._consumer:
            self._consumer.flush_rebalance(run_id, algo=self)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _build_consumer(self) -> Any | None:
        try:
            from services.execution.lean_runtime.signal_consumer import SignalConsumer  # type: ignore[import]
            from services.signal_store.client import SignalStoreClient  # type: ignore[import]
        except ImportError as exc:
            log.error("Cannot import OpenClaw runtime modules: %s — signal consumer disabled", exc)
            return None

        redis_url = os.getenv("SIGNAL_STORE_URL", "redis://signal-store:6379")
        try:
            store = SignalStoreClient(redis_url=redis_url)
            return SignalConsumer(store_client=store)
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("Failed to initialise SignalConsumer: %s — running without signal intake", exc)
            return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stub for non-LEAN environments
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class _ScheduleStub:
    def On(self, *args, **kwargs): pass

"""
OpenClawAlgoBase
================
Base QCAlgorithm class that wires the OpenClaw signal consumer into LEAN.

Responsibilities:
- Bootstrap SignalStoreClient using environment / Object Store config
- Schedule SignalConsumer.drain() every minute
- Expose flush_rebalance() for FinRL batch completion callbacks

This module intentionally imports from the openclaw services path.
When running inside LEAN's Docker container, the services/ directory
is expected to be mounted or installed so that the import resolves.

Import path assumption:
    /app/services/execution/lean-runtime/ must be on PYTHONPATH
    (set this in docker-compose lean service environment or via lean.json pythonVenv)
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import os
from typing import Any

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Guard import so this file can be parsed without LEAN runtime present
try:
    from AlgorithmImports import (  # type: ignore[import]
        QCAlgorithm,
        TimeSpan,
    )
    _LEAN_AVAILABLE = True
except ImportError:
    # Outside LEAN: define a stub base class so unit tests can import this module
    class QCAlgorithm:  # type: ignore[no-redef]
        def Initialize(self): pass
        def Schedule(self): return _ScheduleStub()
    _LEAN_AVAILABLE = False


class OpenClawAlgoBase(QCAlgorithm):
    """
    Subclass this instead of QCAlgorithm to get OpenClaw signal consumption.

    The subclass must call super().Initialize() first, then add its own
    securities and indicators.
    """

    def Initialize(self) -> None:
        self._consumer = self._build_consumer()
        if self._consumer and _LEAN_AVAILABLE:
            self.Schedule.On(
                self.DateRules.EveryDay(),
                self.TimeRules.Every(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)),
                lambda: self._consumer.drain(algo=self),
            )
            log.info("OpenClaw SignalConsumer scheduled (every 1 min)")
        else:
            log.warning("OpenClaw SignalConsumer not available — running without signal intake")

    def flush_rebalance(self, run_id: str) -> None:
        """Call when FinRL signals all legs for a run_id are delivered."""
        if self._consumer:
            self._consumer.flush_rebalance(run_id, algo=self)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Internal
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def _build_consumer(self) -> Any | None:
        try:
            from services.execution.lean_runtime.signal_consumer import SignalConsumer  # type: ignore[import]
            from services.signal_store.client import SignalStoreClient  # type: ignore[import]
        except ImportError as exc:
            log.error("Cannot import OpenClaw runtime modules: %s — signal consumer disabled", exc)
            return None

        redis_url = os.getenv("SIGNAL_STORE_URL", "redis://signal-store:6379")
        try:
            store = SignalStoreClient(redis_url=redis_url)
            return SignalConsumer(store_client=store)
        except Exception as exc:
            log.error("Failed to initialise SignalConsumer: %s — running without signal intake", exc)
            return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Stub for non-LEAN environments
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

class _ScheduleStub:
    def On(self, *args, **kwargs): pass

"""
LP-003: MLflow Registry Adapter.
Maps OpenClaw REG-001 registry entries to MLflow experiment tracking.
"""
import mlflow
from typing import Any, Dict

class MLflowRegistryAdapter:
    def __init__(self, tracking_uri: str, experiment_name: str = "openclaw-strategies"):
        mlflow.set_tracking_uri(tracking_uri)
        mlflow.set_experiment(experiment_name)
        self.version_pin = "2.11.0" # Per OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md

    def log_registry_entry(self, entry: Dict[str, Any], metrics: Dict[str, float] = None):
        """
        Logs a REG-001 registry entry as an MLflow run.
        """
        with mlflow.start_run(run_name=f"{entry['strategy_id']}-v{entry['version']}"):
            # Map Registry Fields to MLflow Params
            mlflow.log_params({
                "strategy_id": entry.get("strategy_id"),
                "version": entry.get("version"),
                "artifact_type": entry.get("artifact_type"),
                "lifecycle_state": entry.get("lifecycle_state"),
                "producer_run_id": entry.get("producer_run_id", "manual")
            })

            # Map Lineage to Tags
            lineage = entry.get("lineage", {})
            mlflow.set_tags({
                "openclaw.source_run_id": lineage.get("source_run_id", "unknown"),
                "openclaw.promotion_state": entry.get("lifecycle_state"),
                "openclaw.checksum": entry.get("checksum", ""),
                "oss.mlflow_version": self.version_pin
            })

            # Log Evaluation Metrics if present
            if metrics:
                mlflow.log_metrics(metrics)
            
            # Log Evaluation Summary as tags or json
            eval_summary = entry.get("evaluation_summary", {})
            if eval_summary:
                for key, val in eval_summary.items():
                    if isinstance(val, (int, float)):
                        mlflow.log_metric(f"eval.{key}", val)

            return mlflow.active_run().info.run_id

    def get_adapter_info(self):
        return {"upstream": "mlflow", "version": self.version_pin}

# AI Collaboration Guide

Last updated: 2026-04-03
Status: canonical collaboration rules for the Pantheon / LEAN repo

## 0. Repository Architecture Decision (2026-04-03)

This repo is currently QuantConnect LEAN + Pantheon services in the same directory.
Note: **OpenClaw** is one of the upstream OSS frameworks Pantheon integrates (like DSPy, Qlib).
**Decision:** migrate to two separate repos:

- `pantheon` — new repo; all of `services/`, `scripts/`, `audits/`, plan docs go here
- `pantheon-lean` — LEAN fork; referenced as a git submodule from `pantheon`

**Until migration completes, the working boundary is:**

| Path | Belongs to | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Root C# dirs (`Engine/`, `Algorithm/`, `Brokerages/`, etc.) | LEAN upstream | Do not modify unless intentional LEAN fork change |
| `Algorithm.Python/pantheon_algo/` | Pantheon ↔ LEAN bridge | Only place Pantheon Python runs inside LEAN |
| `services/` | Pantheon | All agent work happens here |
| `scripts/`, `audits/`, `*.md` plan files | OpenClaw | Move to openclaw repo when ready |

**OSS framework rule:** each named framework (DSPy, Qlib, FinRL, imitation, MLflow) runs in its own Docker container with its own `services/research/<framework>/requirements.txt`. Never merge them into a shared requirements file.

## 1. Canonical Truth

Read these in order before starting work:

1. `AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md`
2. `current-work.md`
3. `ai-status.json`
4. `TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md`
5. `ROADMAP.md`
6. `OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md`
7. `WORK_REBASELINE.md`

Source of truth split:

- `AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md`: stable collaboration rules and command usage
- `ai-status.json`: machine-readable live task state, ownership, blockers, handoffs
- `ai-activity-log.jsonl`: append-only activity history
- `current-work.md`: generated human-readable sprint snapshot
- `TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md`: target-state product architecture
- `ROADMAP.md`: epic-level delivery plan aligned to the target architecture
- `OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md`: execution checklist for named upstream OSS components
- `WORK_REBASELINE.md`: corrected work breakdown and audit scope after reclassifying upstream OSS components
- `docs-site/index.html`: visual collaboration panel

OSS interpretation rule:

- if a document names a real upstream project such as `OpenClaw`, `DSPy`, `Qlib`, `FinRL`, `TRL`, `imitation`, `MLflow`, `W&B`, `RLlib`, or `Tune`, assume that task means upstream integration unless a local replacement is explicitly stated
- do not silently treat upstream project names as conceptual boxes only

Compatibility-only files:

- `COLLAB.md`
- `PROGRESS.md`
- `dashboard.html`
- root `index.html`
- root `ai-status.sh`
- root `ai-status.py`

These are wrappers, not truth.

## 2. Collaboration Model

Separate stable capability lanes from sprint ownership.

### Capability Lanes

- `Claude`: execution plane, control plane, governance review
- `Gemini`: GCP, CI/CD, runtime packaging, worker operations
- `Codex`: integration contracts, status system, schema, acceptance
- `Grok`: coding assist, research ingestion, external search, spec review, critique

Recommended local mode for `Grok`:

- prefer `VS Code` chat if your Grok is exposed there as a coding assistant
- use `Grok Web` / browser chat as fallback when the task is mainly research or external search

# Current Work

This file is generated from `ai-status.json` and `ai-activity-log.jsonl`.
Do not treat this file as the machine-readable source of truth.

```
        integration.md
  scripts/
  audits/
  tools/
  docker-compose.yml               ← 統一編排所有 services
  AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md
  current-work.md
  ai-status.json
  ai-activity-log.jsonl
  TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md
  ROADMAP.md
  OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md
  WORK_REBASELINE.md
  ...（所有計劃文件）

openclaw-lean/                     ← LEAN fork repo（獨立）
  （QuantConnect LEAN 所有 C# 代碼）
  （你們自己的 C# 修改在這裡）
  Algorithm.Python/
    openclaw_algo/                 ← 唯一需要在這裡放的 Python 文件
      signal_consumer_algo.py      ← import signal_consumer，掛入 QCAlgorithm
```

---

## Docker Compose 結構

```yaml
services:
  lean:
    build: ./lean          # submodule Dockerfile
    volumes:
      - ./lean/Data:/Lean/Data
      - ./lean/Launcher/config.json:/app/config.json
    depends_on: [signal-store]

  signal-store:
    image: redis:alpine

  control-plane-router:
    build: ./services/control-plane/router

  control-plane-persona:
    build: ./services/control-plane/persona

  dspy-worker:
    build: ./services/research/dspy     # 只有 dspy-ai 的 requirements.txt

  qlib-worker:
    build: ./services/research/qlib     # 只有 pyqlib 的 requirements.txt

  finrl-worker:
    build: ./services/research/finrl    # 只有 finrl 的 requirements.txt

  imitation-worker:
    build: ./services/research/imitation

  mlflow-server:
    build: ./services/research/mlflow
    ports:
      - "5000:5000"
```

---

## 遷移步驟

### Phase 1：建立新 repo（不影響現有工作）

1. 建立 `openclaw` 新 repo
2. 把現有 `services/`、`scripts/`、`audits/`、所有 Markdown 計劃文件 `git mv` 過去
3. 建立 `openclaw-lean` fork repo（從現有 Lean/ 複製）
4. 在 openclaw 裡用 `git submodule add` 引用 lean fork

### Phase 2：OSS adapter 目錄結構拆分

5. 在 `services/research/` 下為每個 OSS 框架建立獨立子目錄
6. 把 `services/research/requirements.txt` 的單一巨型檔案拆成各框架自己的 `requirements.txt`
7. 為每個框架建立獨立 `Dockerfile`

### Phase 3：LEAN 算法接入點

8. 在 LEAN fork 的 `Algorithm.Python/` 建立 `openclaw_algo/` 目錄
9. 把 `services/execution/lean-runtime/` 打包成可被 QCAlgorithm import 的 Python module
10. 這是唯一需要「活在 LEAN repo 裡」的 Python 代碼

### Phase 4：docker-compose 統一編排

11. 更新根目錄 `docker-compose.yml` 讓所有 service 都能從 openclaw repo 根目錄啟動

---

## 當前工作板的影響

- **不需要重寫任何 Python 邏輯**：services/ 的所有 .py 文件直接搬，不用改代碼
- **需要更新 ai-status.json**：所有 artifact 路徑不變（都在 services/ 下），無需更新
- **需要更新 AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md**：加上 "LEAN fork 是 submodule" 的說明
- **Gemini/Codex 工作不受影響**：他們的任務（REG-002、LP-003 等）針對 services/ 目錄，不依賴 repo 邊界

---

## 關鍵文件路徑

移動前後對比：
| 現在 | 遷移後 |
|---|---|
| `Lean/services/control-plane/router/main.py` | `openclaw/services/control-plane/router/main.py` |
| `Lean/services/research/requirements.txt`（全部框架混在一起） | `openclaw/services/research/dspy/requirements.txt`（各自獨立） |
| `Lean/scripts/ai_status.py` | `openclaw/scripts/ai_status.py` |
| `Lean/Algorithm.Python/（不動）` | `openclaw/lean/Algorithm.Python/openclaw_algo/`（lean submodule 內） |

---

## 驗證方式

1. `git submodule update --init` 能正確 clone lean fork
2. `docker-compose up lean signal-store` 能啟動 LEAN 執行引擎
3. `docker-compose up control-plane-router` 能啟動 router
4. `docker-compose up dspy-worker` 能啟動 DSPy container（不會因為 finrl 依賴衝突而失敗）
5. 跑一個最小 LEAN backtest，確認 signal_consumer 能接收 Redis 信號

## Objective

Align the repo to the governed OpenClaw target architecture where OpenClaw orchestrates workflows, the evolution plane learns through feedback and registry gates, and LEAN executes only approved artifacts.

- Sprint: `2026-04-01-architecture-alignment`
- Canonical files: `AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md`, `current-work.md`, `ai-status.json`, `ai-activity-log.jsonl`, `TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md`, `ROADMAP.md`
- Dashboard: `docs-site/index.html`

# AI Collaboration Guide

Last updated: 2026-04-03
Status: canonical collaboration rules for the Pantheon / LEAN repo

## 0. Repository Architecture Decision (2026-04-03)

This repo is currently QuantConnect LEAN + Pantheon services in the same directory.
Note: **OpenClaw** is one of the upstream OSS frameworks Pantheon integrates (like DSPy, Qlib).
**Decision:** migrate to two separate repos:

- `pantheon` — new repo; all of `services/`, `scripts/`, `audits/`, plan docs go here
- `pantheon-lean` — LEAN fork; referenced as a git submodule from `pantheon`

**Until migration completes, the working boundary is:**

| Path | Belongs to | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Root C# dirs (`Engine/`, `Algorithm/`, `Brokerages/`, etc.) | LEAN upstream | Do not modify unless intentional LEAN fork change |
| `Algorithm.Python/pantheon_algo/` | Pantheon ↔ LEAN bridge | Only place Pantheon Python runs inside LEAN |
| `services/` | Pantheon | All agent work happens here |
| `scripts/`, `audits/`, `*.md` plan files | OpenClaw | Move to openclaw repo when ready |

**OSS framework rule:** each named framework (DSPy, Qlib, FinRL, imitation, MLflow) runs in its own Docker container with its own `services/research/<framework>/requirements.txt`. Never merge them into a shared requirements file.

## 1. Canonical Truth

Read these in order before starting work:

1. `AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md`
2. `current-work.md`
3. `ai-status.json`
4. `TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md`
5. `ROADMAP.md`
6. `OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md`
7. `WORK_REBASELINE.md`

Source of truth split:

- `AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md`: stable collaboration rules and command usage
- `ai-status.json`: machine-readable live task state, ownership, blockers, handoffs
- `ai-activity-log.jsonl`: append-only activity history
- `current-work.md`: generated human-readable sprint snapshot
- `TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md`: target-state product architecture
- `ROADMAP.md`: epic-level delivery plan aligned to the target architecture
- `OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md`: execution checklist for named upstream OSS components
- `WORK_REBASELINE.md`: corrected work breakdown and audit scope after reclassifying upstream OSS components
- `docs-site/index.html`: visual collaboration panel

OSS interpretation rule:

- if a document names a real upstream project such as `OpenClaw`, `DSPy`, `Qlib`, `FinRL`, `TRL`, `imitation`, `MLflow`, `W&B`, `RLlib`, or `Tune`, assume that task means upstream integration unless a local replacement is explicitly stated
- do not silently treat upstream project names as conceptual boxes only

Compatibility-only files:

- `COLLAB.md`
- `PROGRESS.md`
- `dashboard.html`
- root `index.html`
- root `ai-status.sh`
- root `ai-status.py`

These are wrappers, not truth.

## 2. Collaboration Model

Separate stable capability lanes from sprint ownership.

### Capability Lanes

- `Claude`: execution plane, control plane, governance review
- `Gemini`: GCP, CI/CD, runtime packaging, worker operations
- `Codex`: integration contracts, status system, schema, acceptance
- `Grok`: coding assist, research ingestion, external search, spec review, critique

Recommended local mode for `Grok`:

- prefer `VS Code` chat if your Grok is exposed there as a coding assistant
- use `Grok Web` / browser chat as fallback when the task is mainly research or external search
- do not require API automation for normal collaboration
- route it through the same status / handoff system as the other agents

### Sprint Ownership

Current owner, reviewer, dependencies, and next steps live in `ai-status.json`.

Rules:

- each task has exactly one `owner`
- `reviewer` cannot equal `owner`
- blocked tasks must include `waiting_for`
- done transitions must include a checkpoint message
- interface changes should be reflected through status updates, not hidden in chat only

## 3. Status Commands

Use the status script instead of manually editing multiple Markdown tables.

```bash
AI_NAME=Codex ./scripts/ai-status.sh assign <task-id> <owner> <reviewer> "Optional title"
AI_NAME=Codex ./scripts/ai-status.sh start <task-id> "Started implementation"
AI_NAME=Codex ./scripts/ai-status.sh progress <task-id> "Finished contract draft"
AI_NAME=Codex ./scripts/ai-status.sh handoff <task-id> Gemini "Please review the payload shape"
AI_NAME=Codex ./scripts/ai-status.sh blocker <task-id> "Waiting for broker decision" Gemini
AI_NAME=Codex ./scripts/ai-status.sh done <task-id> "Completed and verified"
./scripts/sync-state.sh
```

Command effects:

1. update `ai-status.json`
2. append `ai-activity-log.jsonl`
3. regenerate `current-work.md`
4. mirror state files into `docs-site/`

Optional environment variables:

- `TASK_PHASE`
- `TASK_TITLE`
- `TASK_BRANCH`
- `TASK_ARTIFACTS`
- `TASK_ACCEPTANCE`
- `TASK_DEPENDS_ON`

## 4. Working Agreement

- prefer one source of truth per concern
- do not create a second collaboration tracker outside the canonical files
- use blockers for waits, not ad-hoc side notes
- use handoffs when another agent now owns the next action
- keep long history in `ai-activity-log.jsonl`, not in `current-work.md`
- if a file is a compatibility wrapper, keep it short and point to the canonical path

## 5. Execution Order

Every collaborating LLM should follow this work order by default:

1. **Review first**
- check whether you are currently the `reviewer` for any task that is in `review`
- complete those reviews before starting new implementation work
- if review fails, write the required changes into status and hand the task back clearly

2. **Then do your own assigned work**
- look for tasks where you are the `owner`
- prefer tasks that are `in_progress` first
- then pick tasks that are `todo` but already unblocked by dependencies
- do not idle if one of your assigned tasks is already safe to start

3. **Then help elsewhere**
- if you have no pending reviews and no unblocked owned work, check whether another task is unowned by active work or stalled but still within your capability lane
- if you can safely move it forward, claim it instead of waiting
- when claiming helper work, reassign yourself as `owner` and set the original owner as `reviewer`
- this keeps authorship clear and gives the original owner a structured chance to accept or correct the work

4. **Only then remain blocked**
- if you truly cannot review, cannot advance your own tasks, and cannot safely help another task, log a blocker
- do not stop at "waiting" if useful work is available

### Helper Claim Rule

When helping with a task that was originally assigned to someone else:

1. use `assign` to move the task to yourself
2. set the original owner as the new reviewer
3. leave a clear message in `progress` saying why you claimed it
4. after implementation, `handoff` back to the original owner for review

Example:

```bash
AI_NAME=Codex bash scripts/ai-status.sh assign REG-001 Codex Gemini
AI_NAME=Codex bash scripts/ai-status.sh progress REG-001 "Claimed REG-001 because it is unblocked and can be advanced now; Gemini will review the updated contract."
AI_NAME=Codex bash scripts/ai-status.sh handoff REG-001 Gemini "Registry contract advanced and ready for original-owner review."
```

### Review Completion Rule

A review is not complete until the reviewer does one of these:

- approves by handing off with explicit acceptance
- writes concrete required changes into `review_notes` or task `next`
- records a blocker if review cannot proceed because files or artifacts are missing

Do not leave review feedback only in chat.

## 6. Dashboard

The internal collaboration panel lives at `docs-site/index.html`.

Start it locally with:

```bash
bash scripts/launch-docs-site.sh
```

The dashboard renders:

- workload split
- agent lanes
- task board
- handoff queue
- blockers
- sprint snapshot
- recent activity

If the panel looks stale:

```bash
bash scripts/sync-state.sh
```

## 7. Prompt Prefix

Use this prefix when handing work to any collaborating LLM:

```text
Please read these files before starting:
- AI_COLLABORATION_GUIDE.md
- current-work.md
- ai-status.json
- TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md
- ROADMAP.md
- OSS_INTEGRATION_CHECKLIST.md
- WORK_REBASELINE.md

You are [Claude/Gemini/Codex/Grok].
Follow the current owner/reviewer assignments from ai-status.json.
Update progress through scripts/ai-status.sh instead of manually editing multiple Markdown files.
Work in this order: finish assigned reviews first, then your own unblocked tasks, then claim other safe tasks and set the original owner as reviewer.
```
